title: Reverse an effect to its recorded sources

facts.note: Role (PLT-84), mapped to paths by the structure profile.
The task reverses an earlier consumption or allocation.
Observer: a use case undoes an earlier effect.

fires: Cancelling an operation must give back what it consumed from several sources.
Releasing a reservation drawn from several holdings.
doesNotFire: A fresh credit that is not the reversal of an earlier consumption.

given: An operation consumed quantities from several distinct sources
then: Restore each quantity to the exact source it came from, as recorded at consumption time, applying the rules that hold at reversal time.
prefer: Record per-source allocations (source id, quantity) with the original effect.
Evaluate validity rules (expiry, limits) of each source when reversing, and report what was forfeited.
avoid: Creating a new source with the total instead of restoring the originals.
Restoring into sources that the rules no longer allow, or re-deriving the allocation instead of reading the record.
why: Sources differ in attributes such as expiry or priority; a reversal that does not restore provenance silently changes those attributes.
evidence: A test reverses a multi-source consumption and checks each source.
A test reverses after one source became invalid and checks it is not restored.
